sections.h2: What makes Broomfield different from other Colorado cities?
sections.html:
Broomfield is both a city and a county. It consolidated as the City and County of Broomfield on November 15, 2001, and became Colorado's 64th county, the newest in the state.

It covers about 33.5 square miles and is the smallest county in Colorado by area. Broomfield borders Boulder, Jefferson, Adams and Weld counties. For a seller, one office handles what two would handle elsewhere: the city and county are the same government, so the property tax bill, the recorded deed and the building permit all come back to Broomfield.

sections.h2: Where is Broomfield and how did it begin?
sections.html:
Broomfield sits midway between Denver and Boulder along U.S. Routes 36 and 287, at an elevation of roughly 5,350 feet. The name comes from broomcorn, a sorghum grown in the area, and the post office opened on September 26, 1884.

Railroads shaped the early town: the Colorado Central in 1873, the Denver, Utah and Pacific in 1881 and the Denver, Marshall and Boulder Railway in 1886. The Denver to Boulder Turnpike opened January 19, 1952, with a toll plaza at Broomfield, and it became free on September 14, 1967. Broomfield was incorporated as a city on June 6, 1961.

sections.h2: How big is Broomfield and who lives there?
sections.html:
Broomfield had 74,112 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 79,174 in 2025. It ranks 15th among Colorado municipalities and 12th among Colorado counties by population.

The 2020 density of 2,248 people per square mile was the second highest in Colorado, behind Denver. The median household income in 2024 was reported as $125,055.

Broomfield's largest employer in the city's 2023 annual financial report was Oracle America, with 1,650 employees. Technology drove growth in the 1990s, and the headquarters list includes Crocs, Vail Resorts, Webroot and Noodles and Company.

The employers listed in that report were:

  • Oracle America: 1,650
  • Intermountain Health Care: 1,550
  • BAE Systems: 1,100
  • Hunter Douglas Window Fashions: 950
  • City and County of Broomfield: 900
  • Vail Resorts: 750

A big corporate base brings relocations. Owners who are transferred out of the area on short notice often need to sell faster than a listing cycle allows.

Six districts serve students in Broomfield: Boulder Valley, 27J, Weld County RE-8, Jefferson County, St. Vrain Valley and Adams 12 Five Star. Public schools include Broomfield High and Legacy High, plus two middle schools and eight elementary schools, and two K to 12 charter schools, Prospect Ridge Academy and Front Range Academy.

Because a buyer's school assignment depends on the address, confirm the district for your street before you describe it to a buyer. The city lists Broomfield public schools as two high schools, two middle schools and eight elementary schools, with four private schools also in town.

sections.h2: How does Broomfield's climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Broomfield has a cold semi-arid climate and is in USDA plant hardiness zone 6a. Average annual precipitation is about 16.1 inches. July is the warmest month, with a mean high of 88.7 degrees Fahrenheit, and December has the lowest mean low at 18.0.

Those swings put stress on roofs, exterior paint, fences and sprinkler systems. A listing buyer's inspector will look at each of these, and a cash buyer will price them in without asking you to repair them first.

sections.h2: When are Broomfield property taxes due and how are they paid?
sections.html:
Broomfield taxes can be paid in full by April 30 or in halves on February 28 and June 15. Late payments pick up penalties that rise each month, and a bill under $25 must be paid in full.

  • Payments can be made by cash, check, eCheck or credit card.
  • The card provider fee is 2.50 percent, and an eCheck costs $2.50.
  • The Treasurer is at One DesCombes Drive, and the phone number is 303-464-5810.

Broomfield's treasurer page also describes a Certificate of Taxes Due, which certifies that all property taxes are paid except those listed as still due. The county says it protects purchasers from unlisted prior-year delinquent taxes. Title companies normally request one. See the Broomfield Treasurer page.

sections.h2: How does recording a deed in Broomfield work?
sections.html:
A deed for a Broomfield property is recorded by the City and County Clerk and Recorder, and the fee is a flat $40 plus a $3 surcharge per document. That flat fee took effect July 1, 2025 under HB24-1269 and applies statewide.

Recorded documents are searchable online back to November 2001. Earlier records may be in Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld county, the four counties Broomfield was formed from. The office takes walk-ins and appointments Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and accepts e-recording and mail. It also links the Real Property Transfer Declaration, form TD 1000. Staff cannot give legal advice or search records for you, so a title company usually handles this step. See the Recording page.

Broomfield's city council also serves as the board of county commissioners, and the police chief doubles as the county sheriff.

In practice, a seller can call one set of offices for questions about taxes, recorded documents and local permits. Before you accept any offer, ask the Treasurer or your title company whether any taxes are still owing on the address.

sections.h2: What steps does a cash sale in Broomfield follow?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Broomfield has fewer moving parts than a financed one because no lender approval is needed. The usual order is:

  1. You send us the address and basic details about the house.
  2. We review it and give you a written offer.
  3. A title company opens escrow and orders the Certificate of Taxes Due.
  4. You sign, the deed is recorded with the Broomfield Clerk and Recorder, and funds are released.

You can say no at the offer stage and owe nothing, so asking costs you nothing but a few minutes.

sections.h2: What do Broomfield sellers commonly face?
sections.html:
Broomfield sellers often deal with timing and condition more than demand. Typical situations include:

  • A relocation or job change with a closing date already set
  • An inherited house where heirs live out of state
  • Deferred maintenance on a roof, furnace or water heater
  • A rental that is vacant or has a tenant to resolve

A cash sale lets you set the closing date and skip repairs, showings and a buyer's loan approval. You can still compare it with a listing before you decide.

faqs.q: Is Broomfield a city or a county?
faqs.a: Both. Broomfield became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001, and is Colorado's newest county.

faqs.q: When are Broomfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: The full payment is due April 30. If you pay in halves, the first half is due February 28 and the second half June 15.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Broomfield?
faqs.a: The flat recording fee is $40 plus a $3 surcharge per document, in effect since July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: What is a Certificate of Taxes Due in Broomfield?
faqs.a: It is a certificate from the Treasurer showing that taxes are paid except those listed as due, and it protects buyers from unlisted prior-year delinquencies. Title companies typically order it for a sale.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Broomfield house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address, since six districts serve Broomfield, including Boulder Valley, 27J, Adams 12 Five Star and St. Vrain Valley. Check with the school district or the city before assuming.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Broomfield house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash sale as-is means you do not repair or update the house for a buyer's lender. Review any written offer with your title company or an attorney.
